skills.name: Degree & leading coefficient
skills.wrong_turn: The leading coefficient belongs to the highest power, not the first term written: in 5 + 3x − 2x⁴ it's −2.
skills.rule: The degree is the highest power; the leading coefficient is the number in front of it.

skills.name: End behavior of polynomials
skills.wrong_turn: The sign of the leading coefficient alone doesn't decide the ends. −x³ rises on the left; −x⁴ falls on both sides.
skills.rule: Even degree: ends point the same way. Odd degree: ends point opposite ways. The leading coefficient's sign picks which.

skills.name: Zeros & multiplicity
skills.wrong_turn: In (x − 2)²(x + 1), the zeros are 2 and −1, not −2 and 1. And 2 counts twice.
skills.rule: If (x−a)k is a factor, a is a zero of multiplicity k.

skills.name: Behavior at zeros
skills.wrong_turn: Every zero doesn't cross. At a double root, like x = 2 in (x − 2)², the graph touches and turns back.
skills.rule: At a zero of odd multiplicity the graph crosses the axis; at even multiplicity it bounces.

skills.name: Sketch from factored form
skills.wrong_turn: The y-intercept is f(0), found by plugging in 0: for (x + 2)(x − 1)² it's 2·1 = 2, not −2.
skills.rule: Plot zeros, the y-intercept and the end behaviour, then connect using multiplicity.

skills.name: Turning points
skills.wrong_turn: Degree n allows up to n − 1 turns but doesn't force them: x³ + x has no turning points.
skills.rule: A polynomial of degree n has at most n−1 turning points.

skills.name: Remainder theorem
skills.wrong_turn: Dividing by x + 2 means a = −2, not 2. The remainder is f(−2).
skills.rule: The remainder when f(x) is divided by x−a is f(a).

skills.name: Factor theorem

steps.a: f(a) = 0 means (x − a) is a factor

skills.wrong_turn: A zero at x = 3 gives the factor (x − 3), not (x + 3).
skills.rule: (x−a) is a factor of f(x) exactly when f(a)=0.

skills.name: Rational root theorem
skills.wrong_turn: The theorem only lists candidates. Most of them usually fail; and a polynomial may have no rational roots at all.
skills.rule: A rational root (pq) (lowest terms) of an integer polynomial has p∣a0 and q∣an.

skills.name: Find all zeros
skills.wrong_turn: After dividing out a root, use the quotient for the next search, not the original. Otherwise you keep finding the same root.
skills.rule: Find rational roots first, divide them out, then solve the remaining quadratic for irrational or complex roots.

skills.name: Write a polynomial from zeros
skills.wrong_turn: Zero at −2 gives the factor (x + 2), not (x − 2). And don't forget a to fit the given point.
skills.rule: Zeros ri with multiplicities ki give f(x)=a∏(x−ri)ki; one extra point fixes a.

skills.name: Polynomial inequalities
skills.wrong_turn: Don't divide both sides by x: x³ > 4x is not x² > 4, because x might be negative or zero.
skills.rule: Find the zeros, make a sign chart, and read off the intervals where the inequality holds.

skills.name: Polynomial models
skills.wrong_turn: A model's domain comes from the story: V(x) = x(12 − 2x)² is meaningless for x = 7, even though the formula works.
skills.rule: Build the polynomial from the situation, find its realistic domain, and find the maximum with technology.

skills.name: Roots & coefficients

steps.a: sum and product of quadratic roots
steps.b: build a quadratic from root facts

skills.wrong_turn: The sum of the roots of ax2+bx+c=0 is −(ba), not (ba). For x2−5x+6=0, the roots 2 and 3 sum to 5, not −5.
